```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(repair)
```

## Choose an extractor

The public table extractors let you report results, inspect person-level scores,
and join data without accessing internal S7 slots. All return ordinary data frames
with documented column names, types, keys, and ordering. They introduce no new
fitting choices and do not require a tidyverse or broom dependency.

| Question | Interface |
|---|---|
| What are the structural estimates and intervals? | `repair_coefficients(fit)` |
| What scores and sampling-error SDs were used? | `repair_scores(fit)` |
| How do errors in different scores covary? | `repair_score_covariance(fit)` |
| Which people were excluded? | `repair_diagnostics(fit, table = "excluded")` |
| What are the analysis weights? | `repair_diagnostics(fit, table = "weights")` |
| What is posterior reliability? | `repair_reliability(fit)` |
| What is the covariance of structural coefficient estimates? | `vcov(fit)` |

`coef()`, `vcov()`, `confint()`, `nobs()`, `summary()`, and the existing full
`repair_diagnostics(fit)` list remain available. Score uncertainty, posterior
uncertainty, and structural coefficient uncertainty have different meanings.

## Fit an example

The person-level category below is illustrative, not an actual sleepstudy variable.

```{r fit}
growth <- lme4::lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject), lme4::sleepstudy)
people <- data.frame(person = levels(lme4::sleepstudy$Subject),
                     category = factor(rep(c("A", "B", "C"), 6)))
models <- list(growth = growth)
structural <- re("Days", "growth") ~ re("(Intercept)", "growth") + category
fit <- repair(structural, models, people, id = "person")
```

## Report structural coefficients

```{r coefficient-table}
coefficients <- repair_coefficients(fit)
knitr::kable(coefficients, digits = 3)
repair_coefficients(fit, conf.level = .90)
```

The columns are `term`, `estimate`, `std.error`, `statistic`, `p.value`,
`conf.low`, `conf.high`, and `conf.level`. `term` is character; the remaining
columns are numeric. Rows follow `coef(fit)`, beginning with the structural
intercept. Factor contrast columns retain their model-matrix names. Random-effect
predictors retain model-qualified formula labels. Use these labels as identifiers;
do not parse model or coefficient identity back out of printed text.

Changing `conf.level` changes only the normal interval endpoints and reported
level. Estimates remain on the input scale, and inference remains conditional on
fitted measurement quantities and supplied error covariance. This table does not
standardize coefficients or incorporate additional parameter uncertainty.

## Inspect selected scores

```{r scores}
scores <- repair_scores(fit)
head(scores)
```

The schema is `id`, `model`, `group`, `term`, `label`, `role`, `score`, `std.error`,
`error.variance`, `cohort`, `analyzed`, `status`, and `reason`. Identities, roles,
cohort, and status/reason are character; score and uncertainty columns are numeric;
`analyzed` is logical. The unique key is `(model, group, term, id)`. The qualified
`label` connects random-effect predictors to coefficient-table term labels.
IDs are always character, including originally numeric grouping levels.

Rows follow selected-effect order, then ID order within each effect. Default
`cohort = "analyzed"` uses retained analysis IDs in their person-table order.
`cohort = "measurement"` uses each model's saved effective grouping-level order:

```{r cohorts}
subset_fit <- repair(structural, models, people[3:18, ], "person")
measurement_scores <- repair_scores(subset_fit, cohort = "measurement")
measurement_scores[!measurement_scores$analyzed, c("id", "term", "score", "status")]
```

Only formula-selected effects are returned, even for the measurement cohort.
An excluded person can have an `"ok"` score, for example if an observed structural
predictor was missing. A failed score remains a row with status `"failed"` and a
reason; its saved missing values stay missing. An ID absent from a measurement
model has no score row. Inspect `repair_diagnostics(fit, "excluded")` to find
those IDs and all exclusion reasons.

Scores are **likelihood-only random deviations**. Their `std.error` is a
conditional sampling-error SD, not a BLUP posterior SD, a structural coefficient
SE, or the person's total fixed-plus-random coefficient.

These same score interfaces work before structural fitting:

```{r before-fitting}
assembled <- repair_data(structural, models, people, "person")
stopifnot(identical(repair_scores(assembled), scores))
stopifnot(identical(repair_score_covariance(assembled), repair_score_covariance(fit)))
```

## Preserve covariance when reusing scores

Score variances do not capture correlated errors. The covariance extractor reads
the **assembled** error inputs, including the selected cross-model policy:

```{r covariance}
error_covariance <- repair_score_covariance(fit)
head(error_covariance)
```

Columns are `id`, the two sets of identities `model1`, `group1`, `term1`, `label1`,
`role1` and `model2`, `group2`, `term2`, `label2`, `role2`, followed by numeric
`covariance` and character `source`. All other columns are character. Each pair
appears once per person, including the diagonal. Pairs follow the lower triangle
in selected-effect order: (1,1), (2,1), (2,2), and so on; IDs within a pair follow
analysis order. The key is ID plus the two model/group/term identities.

For multiple models, `source` distinguishes `"within_model"`,
`"assumed_independent"`, and `"supplied"`. An explicitly supplied zero covariance
retains source `"supplied"`. The table includes analyzed IDs only: externally
supplied covariance need not cover excluded people, so there is no measurement-
cohort option. Error-free observed columns are omitted, and their zero error
assumption remains unchanged.

Mirror off-diagonal rows to reconstruct a symmetric selected-effect covariance:

```{r reconstruct}
labels <- unique(scores$label)
one <- error_covariance[error_covariance$id == people$person[1], ]
S <- matrix(0, length(labels), length(labels), dimnames = list(labels, labels))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(one))) {
  S[one$label1[i], one$label2[i]] <- S[one$label2[i], one$label1[i]] <- one$covariance[i]
}
S
```

This is score-error covariance for one person. `vcov(fit)` instead returns the
covariance of estimated structural regression coefficients. Exporting only scores
and treating them as error-free in a later regression would discard REPAIR's
correction. For deliberate custom estimation, see the `fit_mmom()` input contract.

## Select diagnostic tables and join by identity

```{r diagnostics}
repair_diagnostics(fit, table = "cohort")
repair_diagnostics(fit, table = "excluded")
head(repair_diagnostics(fit, table = "weights"))
repair_diagnostics(fit, table = "regularization")
```

The table name must match exactly; no partial matching occurs. Omitting `table`
returns the original diagnostics list. Selecting a table other than reliability
avoids calculating reliability. `cross_model_error` is policy metadata in that
list, not a selectable data frame.

| Table | Columns |
|---|---|
| `status` | converged, step, message |
| `cohort` | n_requested, n_analyzed, n_excluded |
| `excluded` | id, reason |
| `measurement` | model, group, backend, singular, n_measurement, n_outside_requested, messages |
| `score_failures` | model, group, id, analyzed, reason |
| `error_variances` | id, term, role, variance |
| `regularization` | step, policy, alpha, subtraction_multiplier, regularized |
| `conditioning` | step, dimension, min_eigenvalue, max_eigenvalue, condition_number |
| `weights` | id, weight, fraction |
| `weight_summary` | n_people, max_fraction, weight_equivalent_n |
| `reliability` | model, group, term, role, measure, cohort, n_people, n_defined, n_undefined, reliability, mean_defined, min, median, max, status, reason |

All selected tables have automatic row names; IDs and effect names are explicit
columns. Numerical structural failure leaves typed zero-row structural diagnostic
tables, while status and measurement diagnostics remain available. Coefficient
extraction stops on failure; scores and their covariance remain inspectable.

Join scores with marginal posterior reliability using explicit identities and a
matching cohort. Do not join on row number or on `term` alone across models:

```{r join}
reliability <- repair_reliability(fit, level = "person", type = "marginal")
keys <- c("model", "group", "term", "id", "cohort")
joined <- merge(scores, reliability[c(keys, "reliability")], by = keys,
                all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
head(joined[, c("id", "model", "term", "score", "std.error", "reliability")])
stopifnot(nrow(joined) == nrow(scores), !anyNA(joined$reliability))
```

A join may change row order; retain and use the identity columns.

## Export ordinary data frames

No S7-aware serialization or special table package is needed for extracted tables:

```r
write.csv(repair_coefficients(fit), "repair-coefficients.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(repair_scores(fit), "repair-scores.csv", row.names = FALSE)
saveRDS(list(scores = repair_scores(fit),
             score_covariance = repair_score_covariance(fit),
             coefficients = repair_coefficients(fit)), "repair-tables.rds")
```

When importing CSV, read IDs as character to preserve identifiers such as `"001"`.
RDS preserves column types. Keep model specification, cohort choices, and the
cross-model covariance policy with your analysis record. These extractors stabilize
routine reporting and inspection; they do not promise that internal S7 slots will
remain a permanent reporting API.
